learning_outcomes.text: Will know and be able to use basic knowledge about computer science: handling and functions of an operating system, information management with the computer.
Will know and be able to apply fundamental programming notions, allowing the design of small/medium-sized programs.
Will be able to apply valid methodologies/strategies for algorithm development, seeking well-designed solutions.
Will know and be able to use a widely used programming language, preferably one that supports a subsequent object-oriented approach.
Will be able to use abstraction mechanisms as a tool to aid in solving real-world problems.

syllabus_topics: Control structures: iterative composition and sequential processing
Non-elementary data structures: vectors, matrices and pointers
Introduction to the Code::Blocks programming environment
Top-down design (Subprograms: actions and functions) I (seminar)
Top-down design (Subprograms: actions and functions) II (seminar)
assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must achieve at least 50% of the total points and at least 40% in the final written exam. Failure to meet these critical criteria will result in a "Fail" grade, with the final score capped at 4.5 points. Timely submission of assignments is mandatory, and fraudulent actions, including plagiarism, will result in a 0 grade. Part-time students may have non-recoverable activities replaced by equivalent assessments.
